methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $23M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Climate & Energy (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 8 same-sector peers exist in Climate & Energy, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
Windborne, a Series A climate and energy company founded by John Dean, is evaluated against a comp universe of 1 public peer (LNZA) and 8 private companies in the Climate & Energy sector, including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, and KoBold Metals. The target has raised $23.4M to date.

Only one valuation method proved applicable. The Stage-Progression approach, anchored to total capital raised ($23.4M) as a proxy for current valuation, applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A advancement to subsequent stages, yielding $47M. A Peer-Median approach could not be executed: while 8 same-sector peers exist, none satisfied minimum thresholds (≥3 datapoints) when filtered by stage proximity or valuation tier. Applying an all-sector median would introduce uncontrolled heterogeneity and was therefore excluded.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $40M to $54M, with a median of $47M. This range reflects ±15% sensitivity around the stage-progression result. Key uncertainties include the validity of total-raised-as-proxy absent disclosed post-money valuations from the Series A, and the absence of tightly-matched Climate & Energy comparables at the same stage and capital tier. Any revision should incorporate disclosed Series A post-money terms or additional private market transactions in hardware-intensive energy sectors.
